postTitle: Tax-Loss Harvesting and Asset Location Explained
topic: A fall in value only becomes a loss for tax when the investment is sold

assumptions.notes: Reel's own small example, illustrative: bought for €1,000, worth €800, sold for €800: a recorded loss of €200. The lesson's larger example (a €10,000 loss offsetting a €10,000 gain) is in the caption.

caption.instagram:
You paid €1,000 and your investment is now worth €800. Does that fall lower your tax?

Not on its own. A fall in value is only a number on a screen until the investment is sold. Selling for €800 records a €200 loss. Where the rules allow, a recorded loss can reduce the profit counted for tax on another sale, in the same year or a later one.

Two things the reel leaves for the lesson. People who sell at a loss often buy something similar straight away, so their money stays invested; in many countries, buying the same thing straight back means the loss does not count yet. And the tax is usually delayed, not removed: the replacement was bought at a lower price, so a later sale can show a bigger profit.
